questions.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $U$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-10,10],$ compute $P(U<-3).$
questions.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $U$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(u)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le u\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $U$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-10,10],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(u)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{20},\, & -10\le u\le 10, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(U<-3) & =P(-10\le U<-3) \\  & ={\int }_{-10}^{-3}f(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{-10}^{-3}\frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{-3-(-10)}{20} \\  & =\frac{7}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-3,1],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}, & -3\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2\le X\le 2) & =P(-2\le X\le 1) \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1-(-2)}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ compute $P(0\le X\le \frac{3\pi }{4}).$
questions.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2\pi },\, & -\pi \le x\le \pi , \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X\le \frac{3\pi }{4}) & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /4}\frac{1}{2\pi }\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3\pi }{4}-0)}{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ follows a **continuous uniform distribution** on the interval $[a,b]$ if all values of $X$ are equally likely on $[a,b].$

Intuitively, the familiar statement "choose a random number between $a$ and $b$" can be translated as "observe a value from the continuous uniform distribution on $[a,b].$" 

The probability density function for the continuous uniform distribution on an interval $[a,b]$ takes the following form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14128799/assets/a247cacd484a99d579d2a30245d7ab495f6d0d116fbf02e2fe8a95fa658df9c6.svg)

This corresponds to the following graph:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14128799/assets/9d077084b025c673533cefc52b7d2e7bfe90e8f903e926a27ce8d1207a0d4e79.png)

Notice that the probability density of the continuous uniform distribution on $[a,b]$ is just $1$ divided by the length of the interval. This ensures that our probability density function has the same value everywhere in the interval and integrates to $1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{1}{b-a}\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{x}{b-a}|}_{a}^{b} \\  & =\frac{b-a}{b-a} \\  & =1\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

When a random variable $X$ follows a continuous uniform distribution on the interval $[a,b],$ we often write

$$
X\sim U[a,b]
$$

 

and say that "$X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[a,b].$"
